# Glossary — Forest vocabulary (EN)

> Canonical multilingual vocabulary of the `.roots` / Forest model. Generated from `glossary.json` — do not edit by hand; run `gen.py`.
>
> English is the primary language (the key). Spanish/French are translations.

## Forest metaphor

| Term | Definition | See also |
|---|---|---|
| **Roots** | The `.roots/` folder: the persistent memory/knowledge layer that lives with the code (context, decisions, journal, tasks, skills, docs). The metaphor starts here and grows upward. | Forest · seed |
| **Forest** | The whole workspace — every coordinated repo. The folder that contains the repos. Modeled by `forest.json` in workspace mode. | Grove · Tree · Workspace mode · forest.json |
| **Grove** | A product / suite: a cluster of Trees with a common function (e.g. Meli, OCAPI, GeoEcon). A Tree's primary grove answers 'what it is'. | Forest · Tree · grove (axis) |
| **Tree** | A repo, mounted bare + worktrees (e.g. `meli_oerp`, `geoecon_map`). Described by orthogonal axes: grove, vendor, kind, org. | Branch · Grove · vendor · kind |
| **Branch** | A git branch / worktree of a Tree (e.g. `17.0`, `mapdev`). One worktree per branch under the bare+worktrees pattern. | Tree · branch (primitive) |
| **Folio (Leaf)** | The `folios/` folder: a document turned **outward** — published, exposed, seen. *Folio* is *folium*: leaf. What separates it from `roots/` is direction, not material: the same document has an inner face (memory) and an outer face (folio). A folio hangs from a **branch** (you publish a version, not a project) and is a **view, never a second original**: its substance stays in the `.roots/` document it is the face `of:`. | Roots · Branch · Reception (Photosynthesis) |
| **Leaf (leaves/)** | The **sixth term** of the Forest vocabulary and the only one that names what must **go**: an *ephemeral* session artifact (a DOM snapshot, a verification capture, a raw API dump). It is the organ of exchange with the outside — the instant a session touched something external and kept the evidence. It hangs from a **Branch** (a task), not from the Forest, lives in `workbench/leaves/<date>-<front>/` and is **designed to fall**. The rule: *before the leaf falls, what it taught must already have gone down into `.roots/`*. A leaf kept is a **folio**; a leaf shed is litter → humus → root. | Folio (Leaf) · workbench/ · leaf fall · Branch |
| **Reception (Photosynthesis)** | `folios/<slug>/reception.md`: what came back from a published folio — what was asked, cited, misread, requested, who got in touch. It is the **only thing that enters a project from the outside**, and by default it lands nowhere. What it teaches is promoted inward: a recurring question becomes documentation, a recurring misreading becomes an ADR, a demand becomes a task. It closes the cycle: material in → memory down → structure up → leaf out → reception back down. | Folio (Leaf) · collective/ · workbench/ |

## Tree axes

| Term | Definition | See also |
|---|---|---|
| **vendor** | Authorship/ownership axis of a Tree (`vendor: <slug>`, e.g. `moldeo-interactive`, `oca`, `odoo-sa`). A field, not a structural node; may have an optional profile at `.roots/vendors/<slug>.md`. | Tree · kind · grove (axis) |
| **relations[]** | A directed graph (DAG) of dependencies between Trees/modules/services: `{from, to, type}` with types `depends-on`, `extends`, `integrates`, `relates`. Dependencies are edges — NEVER nesting or tags. | Tree · golden rule (graph) |
| **grove (axis)** | The primary-product axis of a Tree (cardinality: exactly 1). Answers 'what is it part of'. | Grove · also_groves · golden rule (graph) |
| **also_groves** | Optional tags (0..N) of genuine co-membership in another product — NOT a dependency. The 'also a part of' tag in the golden rule. | grove (axis) · golden rule (graph) |
| **kind** | The nature of a Tree (cardinality 1). Enum: `product-suite`, `platform` (abstract base others depend on), `aggregator` (deployment nesting modules from many Groves), `external-upstream` (vendored: Odoo core, OCA), `seed` (roots tooling). | Tree · vendor |
| **org** | The hosting axis of a Tree (cardinality 1): where the repo lives (the hosting org/namespace). Distinct from `vendor` (who authors it). | Tree · vendor |
| **golden rule (graph)** | `grove` = what it IS · edge (`relations[]`) = what it USES · tag (`also_groves`) = what it's ALSO part of. Dependencies are always edges, never membership or nesting. | grove (axis) · relations[] · also_groves |
| **branch (primitive)** | One of the 3 reusable primitives (vendor · relations[] · branch). A fork carrying `stage`/`merged_into`/`created_by: human\|AI`: a git branch, a design variant, or a story arc. | Branch · vendor · relations[] |

## Working modes

| Term | Definition | See also |
|---|---|---|
| **Flat mode** | The default, simplest layout: `.roots/` directly at the root, no internal namespace. For a single-project repo with few/no embedded remote sources. | Source mode · Client-branch mode · Workspace mode |
| **Source mode** | Namespaced layout `.roots/{module}/` for a multi-module source repo (the source of truth for several modules). | Flat mode · Client-branch mode |
| **Client-branch mode** | Namespaced layout `.roots/{context}.{project}/` for a client branch that consumes/embeds one or more sources. Uses the full multi-source machinery. | Source mode · embedded source · _sources.json |
| **Workspace mode** | A `.roots/` that does not document one project but coordinates N repos from the folder that contains them (the Forest). Golden rule: index and point, do not duplicate. | Forest · forest.json |
| **Migration mode** | A flat repo may temporarily fork into namespaced during a migration (e.g. `.roots/17.0/` + `.roots/19.0/` side by side) and collapse back to flat on the new version. | Flat mode |
| **domain pack** | A domain overlay (e.g. `working_mode: narrative`) layered on top of any base mode, adding domain-specific folders (worldbible, character sheets, arcs as branches). | Workspace mode |

## Multi-source machinery

| Term | Definition | See also |
|---|---|---|
| **embedded source** | A copy of a source's `.roots/` placed under `sources/` in a client branch, linked via `_sources.json`. Lets the client carry the source's memory locally. | _sources.json · precedence cascade · Client-branch mode |
| **_sources.json** | The manifest that links embedded sources to their originals: source ids, paths, `last_sync`, and `sync_include`/`sync_exclude` rules. | embedded source · precedence cascade |
| **precedence cascade** | Resolution order when the same knowledge exists at multiple levels: root client > embedded source > original source. | embedded source · conflict namespace |
| **conflict namespace** | Pattern `source.skill_name` to disambiguate same-named items across sources, with client overrides taking precedence. | precedence cascade · discovery promotion |
| **discovery promotion** | Semi-automatic promotion of a discovery made in the client back to the original source (e.g. a reusable skill, a fix, a decision). | embedded source · upstream sync |

## Registries & metadata

| Term | Definition | See also |
|---|---|---|
| **context_format** | A registered, domain-specific context schema declared in `_meta.json` (Odoo is the first: `{major}.{minor}.{infra}.{project}`). Lets the agent reason about the environment without guessing. | context_parsed · _meta.json |
| **context_parsed** | The parsed object form of `context_format` in `_meta.json` (e.g. `{major:17, minor:0, infra:'sh', project:'acme'}`). Metadata for reasoning, independent of the directory layout. | context_format · _meta.json |
| **forest.json** | The structured registry of the Forest (workspace mode): `vocabulary`, `groves[]`, `vendors[]`, `repos[]` (Trees with grove/vendor/kind/org) and `relations[]`. Rename of `fleet.json`. | Forest · fleet.json · relations[] |
| **fleet.json** | The former name of `forest.json`, kept as a compatibility symlink so older tools / the forest-dashboard (which read `repos[]`) keep working. | forest.json |
| **_meta.json** | Per-`.roots/` state file: `seed_version`, `layout`, `working_mode`, `lang`, `context_format`/`context_parsed`, `project`, `modules`, `sources`, `current_feature`. | context_format · lang · working_mode |
| **working_mode** | The `_meta.json` field that records the chosen mode (`source`, `client`, `workspace`, optionally a domain like `narrative`). Decided once on seed-process, never re-asked. | _meta.json · Flat mode · Workspace mode |

## Memory layers (.roots files)

| Term | Definition | See also |
|---|---|---|
| **context.md** | The 30-second briefing of a `.roots/`: what it is, stack, current state, key conventions, critical dependencies. Read first on session-start. | Roots |
| **glossary.md (per-module)** | The domain glossary of a single `.roots/`: project-specific terms, written in the deployment's working language. Distinct from the seed's multilingual `glossary/` of Forest vocabulary. | glossary system · context.md |
| **workbench/** | The **local work surface** inside `.roots/`: raw material the human shares, drafts the agent produces, heavy assets, and `leaves/`. It lives inside `.roots/` precisely so it does not mix with the visible versioned tree, and it is **entirely out of git**. Nothing durable lives only here. If something on the surface deserves versioning, it is **moved out** — never whitelisted back in. *(Corrected in 1.19: until then it was described as the user's folder with a selective ignore, which is the opposite of real use and silently fills a repo.)* | Leaf (leaves/) · collective/ · leaf fall |
| **collective/** | Permanent memory of the third-party influences/references that feed the project (people, ideas, sites, works, organizations, books), with attribution. The permanent counterpart of `workbench/`. | workbench/ |

## Seed distribution

| Term | Definition | See also |
|---|---|---|
| **seed** | The master template (`roots_seed.md`) that defines the `.roots/` format, style standards and population protocols. Each `.roots/` carries a local copy to be self-contained. | canonical · distribution (seed) · upstream sync |
| **canonical** | The single editable source of the seed (the module that maintains it). Distributed copies carry a header pointing back to the canonical; diff = pending delta to apply. | seed · distribution (seed) · upstream sync |
| **distribution (seed)** | The mandatory rule that every `.roots/` carries a copy of the seed as `.roots/roots_seed.md`, making the module self-contained and reprocessable. | seed · canonical |
| **upstream sync** | Always check the public upstream `github.com/ctmil/roots_seed` before using/processing a seed copy — it may be a distributed, outdated copy. Compare the `Version`/changelog. | canonical · seed |
| **capability ladder** | How a command publishes upstream without depending on a tool the reader happens to have: an authenticated CLI → an API token → a **prefilled issue URL, which always works with no credentials**. The command **declares which rung it used**, and the rule that goes with it: ⛔ never report an issue as «opened» when only a URL was printed — and publishing, being an outward action, goes out with an explicit confirmation, never as a side effect of drafting. | upstream sync · canonical |

## Token economy

| Term | Definition | See also |
|---|---|---|
| **layer ladder (L0–L3)** | Read by layers, not everything: L0 index → L1 active slice → L2 domain doc → L3 corpus. The core of the token economy. | CER · FS · tier (budget) |
| **CER** | Context Efficiency Ratio = useful / loaded tokens. How much of what you loaded actually got used. | FS · layer ladder (L0–L3) · tier (budget) |
| **FS** | Frugality Score = if_I_read_everything / loaded. How much you saved by reading in layers instead of loading the whole corpus. | CER · layer ladder (L0–L3) |
| **tier (budget)** | The task budget tier that sets how deep to read: trivial / normal / deep / full. | CER · FS |

## Lifecycle hooks

| Term | Definition | See also |
|---|---|---|
| **sync semaphore** | A multi-session lock (`.SYNCING` flag per module) so concurrent sessions on the same source don't clobber each other's uncommitted changes. Helper: `sync-lock.sh`. | Workspace mode |
| **on-seed-process** | The master hook run when processing/reprocessing a seed: detect mode and language, upstream sync, distribution, source sync, CLAUDE.md verification, workbench check. | on-seed-update · lang · working_mode |
| **on-seed-update** | The hook run when the canonical seed version is bumped: re-distribute the local copy to every `.roots/`. Never rewrites or translates existing memory. | on-seed-process · distribution (seed) |
| **leaf fall** | The scheduled sweep of ephemeral artifacts: `leaf-fall.sh` `status` (litter loose on the Forest floor) · `sweep` (into today's `leaves/`) · `compost [days]`. Reframing the cleanup as a *season* rather than as *tidying up a mess* is what makes it happen — and **hygiene warns, it does not block**: a check that rejects a commit gets bypassed with `--no-verify`. | Leaf (leaves/) · workbench/ |
| **work semaphore (claim)** | The second lock: the `sync semaphore` protects **worktrees** (files), this one protects **the work** (the subject) — that two sessions do not take the same front without knowing. One `<scope>.claim` file per subject, out of git. Before entering a front: `check`; held by someone else and fresh → do not touch, leave your note on the bus for the owner. Helper: `work-claim.sh`. | sync semaphore · session liveness · declared loop |
| **session liveness** | Whether the session holding a claim still exists — a **verifiable fact** (does its runtime socket exist?), not an inference from elapsed time, because `by=` is a **role** that several tabs share. It changes what *stale* means: **STALE + DEAD** = free to take; **STALE + ALIVE** = someone is working and did not check in → **do not take it**. ⚠️ A liveness probe must **detect itself first**: one that cannot see its own session reports `?`, never DEAD — a guessed probe once reported 16 of 16 dead, including its own caller. | work semaphore (claim) · declared loop |
| **declared loop** | The `loop=<name>@<interval>` field of a claim: whether that front **gets looked at again by itself**, and how often. It is **declared, not detected** (nothing in the environment reveals a running loop), and kept honest two ways: a loop declared by a dead session prints with a warning, and every heartbeat rewrites it. Read it together with the heartbeat **series**, not one value: **a gap is judged against the front's own cadence, never a global threshold** — 43 minutes of silence on a front that beats every 20 is 2.9× its own period, while an 8-hour staleness limit would arrive 24 times too late. | work semaphore (claim) · session liveness |
| **delivery layer** | The half of the memory that 1.19 added: not how it is **stored** but how it **reaches** the agent. Written rules failed three times the same way — the bus nobody read, five dated rules violated with the documents open, a contribution policy that sat as prose for fifteen versions. The cause is structural: **documents are selected by TOPIC, and normative documents do not talk about the topic** — they talk about the form of the work. ⇒ **a rule in a file nobody loads does not happen**: the memory must not be searched, it must **arrive**. Three invariants: inject don't block · everything in try/except · the registry is data, not code. | inbox delivery · session minutes · context guard |
| **inbox delivery** | Putting the session's claims and its **open** bus messages in front of it on every prompt, instead of asking it to go and fetch them. Its routing rule is what makes the bus usable: a message reaches the session whose `to:` names it **or any scope it holds a claim on** — so another session can write to a scope **without knowing which tab is handling it**. | delivery layer · work semaphore (claim) |
| **session minutes** | A record left **before** the context is compacted. It matters because the compaction summary is written **by the agent**, which makes it exactly what the human cannot audit: if the agent was wrong, the summary inherits the error and becomes the only surviving version of events. **The minutes are not a summary, they are a RECORD** — drawn from the transcript, listing verifiable facts (what was asked, what ran, which files changed, which commits and messages went out, with their ids). No narrative. **If the minutes and the agent's account disagree, the minutes win.** They append per session: the point is the whole series. | delivery layer · context guard |
| **context guard** | A two-step warning **before** the context fills. Without it the only signal is the compaction **already done** — the warning arrives after the damage. Delegates the measurement to a script instead of duplicating it, and **does not block**: a hook that cuts the work mid-batch costs more than the problem it solves. | session minutes · delivery layer |

## Language & i18n

| Term | Definition | See also |
|---|---|---|
| **lang** | The `_meta.json` field that records the working language of a `.roots/` deployment (`en` default, `es`, `fr`, …). Code/technical identifiers are always English regardless of `lang`. | glossary system · language lock · _meta.json |
| **language lock** | The no-noise rule: the canonical seed is English, but each deployment keeps its own `lang`. On seed-process the agent auto-detects the language of existing `.roots/` content and persists it; updating/redistributing the seed NEVER translates or rewrites existing memory. | lang · on-seed-process · on-seed-update |
| **glossary system** | The seed's multilingual vocabulary at `glossary/`: `glossary.json` (canonical, EN key + es/fr) generates `GLOSSARY.<lang>.md` tables via `gen.py`. Gives consistent Forest terminology in any `lang`. | lang · glossary.md (per-module) · language lock |
